input.candidate_text:
Assume for contradiction that \(x>1\). Taking \(n=2\) gives
\[
4y^2+1\mid x-1.
\]
Choose a prime \(p\mid 4y^2+1\). This number is odd, and \(3\nmid 4y^2+1\), since \(4y^2+1\equiv y^2+1\not\equiv0\pmod3\). Hence \(p\ge5\). Set
\[
a=v_p(x-1)\ge1
\]
and choose an integer \(k>a\).

Let \(f(T)=y^2T^2+1\). We have \(f(2)\equiv0\pmod p\), while
\[
f'(2)=4y^2\not\equiv0\pmod p.
\]
Thus, by the elementary Hensel lifting argument, there exists \(r\) such that
\[
r\equiv2\pmod p,\qquad f(r)\equiv0\pmod{p^k}.
\]
Consequently \(s=-r\) also satisfies \(f(s)\equiv0\pmod{p^k}\), and \(s\equiv-2\equiv p-2\pmod p\).

Put \(b=(p-1)^2\). Since
\[
b-1=p(p-2),
\]
we have \(v_p(b-1)=1\). By LTE,
\[
v_p(b^m-1)=1+v_p(m)
\]
for every positive integer \(m\). Hence \(b\) has order \(p^{k-1}\) modulo \(p^k\), so it generates the subgroup of units congruent to \(1\pmod p\).

Now \(s(p-2)^{-1}\equiv1\pmod p\). Therefore, for some \(t\ge0\),
\[
b^t\equiv s(p-2)^{-1}\pmod{p^k}.
\]
Define
\[
n=(p-2)b^t=(p-2)(p-1)^{2t}.
\]
Then \(n\equiv s\pmod{p^k}\), and hence
\[
p^k	ext{ divides }n^2y^2+1.
\]
Every prime divisor of \(n\) divides either \(p-2\) or \(p-1\), so it is strictly smaller than \(p\). From the prime-factor formula for Euler’s totient, it follows that
\[
p\nmid\varphi(n).
\]

By the hypothesis,
\[
n^2y^2+1\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1,
\]
so \(p^k\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1\). On the other hand, since \(p\) is odd and \(p\mid x-1\), LTE gives
\[
v_p\bigl(x^{\varphi(n)}-1\bigr)
=v_p(x-1)+v_p(\varphi(n))=a<k,
\]
a contradiction. Therefore \(x>1\) is impossible. Since \(x\) is a positive integer, \(x=1\).

problem.theorem:
Let \( x \) and \( y \) be positive integers. If for each positive integer \( n \) we have that

\[
(n y)^{2}+1 \mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1
\]

prove that \( x=1 \).
